mainTopic: The ערבה (its source, rules, שיעור, and no ברכה), teachings of אייבו in the name of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, and the start of the משנה on the לולב in the מקדש
overview: This amud opens by settling a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's words. The ערבה in the מקדש is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and the ערבה in the גבולין is a תקנת נביאים. רבי אמי then gives three rules: the ערבה needs a שיעור, it is taken by itself, and the ערבה tied into the לולב does not count, even if the לולב is lifted a second time. רב חסדא in the name of רבי יצחק disagrees. On the שיעור, רב נחמן requires three twigs with moist leaves, and רב ששת requires only one leaf on one twig. Stories about רבי אלעזר בר צדוק and רב show that the ערבה is waved without a ברכה, because it is a מנהג נביאים. Through more teachings from אייבו, the גמרא tells of a man worried about villagers hoeing his groves in שביעית and eating his olives. The גמרא explains that hoeing to seal cracks is permitted. It then gives a rule against traveling more than three פרסאות on ערב שבת, with two versions of רב כהנא's comment. Finally it returns to the משנה about arranging the לולבים on the bench in the מקדש, and רב נחמן's reaction to a recited version continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One statement is about the Temple, the other about the outlying areas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction between רבי יוחנן's two statements about ערבה. One is about the מקדש and one is about the גבולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is speaking about the Temple; there it is speaking about the outlying areas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion. It explains that רבי יוחנן's two statements about ערבה do not clash, because each one is about a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן said the ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and he also said it is a תקנת נביאים. The answer: the ערבה in the מקדש comes from Sinai. The ערבה taken in the גבולין (everywhere outside the מקדש) was set up by the prophets.

keyTerms.meaning: Here / in this case. A word used to divide two cases apart.
The outlying areas, meaning everywhere outside the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: ערבה in the מקדש = הלכה למשה מסיני. ערבה in the גבולין = תקנת נביאים.

phrases.english: Here, in the Temple;
phrases.notes: In the Temple, the ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

phrases.english: there, in the outlying areas.
phrases.notes: Outside the Temple, the ערבה is a תקנת נביאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction earlier between רבי יוחנן's two statements about ערבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement applies to a different location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to contradict himself about where the ערבה law comes from.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no contradiction. The מקדש ערבה is from Sinai, and the גבולין ערבה is from the prophets.

steps.title: רבי אמי's three rules about the willow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי gives three rules. The ערבה needs a minimum size, it must be taken by itself, and the ערבה tied into the לולב does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: The willow needs a minimum size. It is taken only by itself. And a person does not fulfill his obligation with the willow that is in the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רבי אמי states three rules about the special ערבה מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the separate ערבה מצוה, not the two ערבות tied into the ארבעה מינים. רבי אמי says it needs a שיעור, it must be lifted on its own, and the ערבה already bound in the לולב cannot be used for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A required minimum size or amount
His obligation (as in fulfilling the מצוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of ערבה. The ערבה tied in the לולב is part of the ארבעה מינים. This discussion is about the separate ערבה מצוה, which is taken on its own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
The willow requires a minimum measure,
and it is taken only by itself,
and a person does not fulfill his obligation
with the willow that is in the lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי עֲרָבָה צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the practical rules of the ערבה מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבה needs a שיעור, must be taken separately, and the ערבה in the לולב does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: Isn't the third rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אמי needed his third rule. If the ערבה must be taken by itself, then obviously the ערבה in the לולב does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said it is taken only by itself, it is obvious that a person does not fulfill his obligation with the willow in the לולב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי's wording. It says his third rule seems to repeat his second rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule two says the ערבה must be taken בפני עצמה. That already seems to exclude the ערבה inside the לולב. So rule three looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master. A respectful way of referring to the speaker, here רבי אמי.
It is obvious! A challenge saying a statement adds nothing new.

phrases.english: Since the Master said
it is taken only by itself,
it is obvious that a person does not fulfill [his obligation]
with the willow that is in the lulav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the third clause of רבי אמי's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The third clause of רבי אמי: the ערבה in the לולב does not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition (פשיטא): this clause seems already included in the second clause.

steps.title: The third rule covers lifting the lulav a second time
steps.stepSummary: The third rule teaches something new. Even if a person lifts the לולב a second time on purpose for the ערבה מצוה, the ערבה inside it still does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that rule applies only when he did not lift it and then lift it again. But if he lifted it and then lifted it again, say no [he does fulfill]. So it teaches us [that even then he does not].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the third rule rules out a case we might have thought was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought: lifting the לולב once does not count for the ערבה, because it is one action for the לולב. But if he lifts it a second time just for the ערבה, perhaps that counts as taking it on its own. רבי אמי teaches that even then it does not count. The ערבה must be physically separate.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. Introduces a mistaken assumption.
He lifted it and then lifted it again
It teaches us. Introduces the new point.

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'אימא לא' ('say no') belong to the mistaken thought. They mean 'say the rule does not apply', that is, he would fulfill the מצוה. קא משמע לן rejects that.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies only where
he did not lift it and then lift it again,
but if he lifted it and then lifted it again,
say no [the rule does not apply, and he fulfills],
so he teaches us [that even then he does not].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by pointing to a new case the third rule covers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the clause blocks a reasonable but mistaken assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lifting the לולב a second time just for the ערבה might count as taking it separately.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a second lifting does not help. The ערבה must be taken physically on its own.
steps.whatToRemember: The ערבה inside the לולב never counts for the ערבה מצוה, according to רבי אמי, even if the לולב is lifted again for that purpose.

steps.title: רב חסדא in רבי יצחק's name: the לולב's willow does count
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes רבי יצחק, who disagrees with רבי אמי. A person does fulfill his obligation with the ערבה in the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: A person fulfills his obligation with the willow that is in the לולב (on the first day of the festival).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opposite opinion. Here the ערבה tied in the לולב is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This directly argues with רבי אמי's third rule. The words in parentheses ('on the first day of the festival') are marked in the printed text as a doubtful addition. The core point is the disagreement itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The first festival day of סוכות

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak:
A person fulfills his obligation
with the willow that is in the lulav
(on the first festival day of the holiday).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a view that argues with רבי אמי's third rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One does fulfill the ערבה obligation with the ערבה in the לולב.

steps.title: What is the willow's minimum size?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי אמי's first rule and asks how big the ערבה must be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is its measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the שיעור רבי אמי mentioned. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said the ערבה needs a שיעור but did not give the amount. This question opens a discussion to fill in that detail.

phrases.english: And how much is its measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first clause of רבי אמי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact minimum size of the ערבה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: three twigs with moist leaves
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the minimum is three twigs that have fresh, moist leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Three twigs with moist leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the first answer to the question about the שיעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things are required: the number of twigs (three) and the condition of the leaves (moist, not dried out).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Three twigs of moist leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.

steps.title: רב ששת: even one leaf and one twig
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives a much smaller minimum. As first quoted, he says even one leaf and one twig.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: Even one leaf and one twig.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second, more lenient answer about the שיעור. The גמרא will question his exact wording next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת argues with רב נחמן and allows a far smaller ערבה. As quoted, his words seem to describe a loose leaf plus a separate twig, which sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Even one leaf and one twig.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer that argues with רב נחמן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even one leaf and one twig (wording to be corrected).

steps.title: A loose leaf and a separate twig? That can't be right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב ששת's wording. It makes no sense that a detached leaf plus a separate twig would count.
steps.simpleTranslation: One leaf and one twig, would that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב ששת's statement. It cannot mean a leaf and a twig as two separate items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'one leaf and one twig' sounds like two separate objects. A loose leaf is not a branch at all, so the wording cannot be what he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? Shows that an idea is unreasonable.

phrases.english: One leaf and one twig
would that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: עָלֶה אֶחָד וּבַד אֶחָד סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks how רב ששת's statement is worded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'עלה אחד ובד אחד' in רב ששת's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Logical impossibility: a separate leaf and twig cannot make up a valid ערבה.

steps.title: Correct it: even one leaf on one twig
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רב ששת's wording. He means one twig that still has one leaf on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: Even one leaf on one twig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב ששת's words to remove the problem. This settles his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'and' (ו) to 'on' (ב) changes the meaning. Instead of two separate items, it is a single twig with at least one leaf still attached. That is רב ששת's lenient minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. Introduces a corrected reading.

steps.whatToRemember: The שיעור of ערבה: רב נחמן requires three twigs with moist leaves. רב ששת requires only one twig with one leaf on it.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Even one leaf on one twig.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת meant a separate leaf and a separate twig.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ששת meant one twig with one leaf attached.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק waves the willow without a blessing
steps.stepSummary: אייבו reports that רבי אלעזר בר צדוק took a ערבה, waved it, and made no ברכה. The גמרא explains that he held it is a מנהג נביאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אייבו said: I was standing before רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, and a man brought him a ערבה. He took it and waved it, waved it, but did not make a ברכה. This shows he held that the ערבה is a custom started by the prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the size of the ערבה to how it is used. It tells a story showing that a great sage did not say a ברכה on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה is said on a מצוה commanded by the Torah or by the Rabbis. A custom of the prophets is weaker than that. So רבי אלעזר בר צדוק waved the ערבה but did not say a ברכה. The words 'קסבר' show that the גמרא is explaining why he acted this way.

keyTerms.meaning: He beat or waved it (striking the ערבה)
A custom set up by the prophets, not a full מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practice of taking the ערבה on הושענא רבה without a ברכה.

phrases.english: Aivu said:
phrases.notes: אייבו was the father of רב

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק
phrases.english: I was standing before Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok
and a certain man brought a willow branch before him.
He took it, waved and waved it, and did not recite a blessing.
He holds that it is a custom of the prophets.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is explaining his view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַיְיבוּ: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the minimum size of the ערבה to how it is taken and whether a ברכה is said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבה is waved without a ברכה, because it is a מנהג נביאים.

steps.title: רב also waves the willow without a blessing
steps.stepSummary: A matching story about רב: his grandsons brought him a ערבה, and he waved it without a ברכה, for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: אייבו and חזקיה, the sons of רב's daughter, brought a ערבה to רב. He waved it, waved it, and did not make a ברכה. He also held that it is a custom of the prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second story with the same practice. This shows that רב agreed with רבי אלעזר בר צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two authorities, a תנא and an אמורא, acting the same way. This strengthens the rule that no ברכה is said on the ערבה. The explanation is the same: it is a מנהג נביאים.
steps.confusionAlert: This אייבו is רב's grandson, not the אייבו from the first story, who was רב's father.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי אלעזר בר צדוק and רב waved the ערבה without a ברכה, because it is a מנהג נביאים.

phrases.english: Aivu and Ḥizkiya, sons of Rav's daughter,
brought a willow branch before Rav.
He waved and waved it, and did not recite a blessing.
He holds that it is a custom of the prophets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְיבוּ וְחִזְקִיָּה בְּנֵי בְרַתֵּיה דְּרַב אַיְיתוֹ עֲרָבָה לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that supports the same practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב also waved the ערבה without a ברכה, treating it as a מנהג נביאים.

steps.title: A landowner asks about villagers working his trees in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: Since אייבו was the reporter above, the גמרא brings another story he told. A man asks רבי אלעזר בר צדוק whether it is proper that villagers hoe his groves and eat his olives, apparently during שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אייבו said: I was standing before רבי אלעזר בר צדוק. A man came and said: I have villages, groves, and olives. The villagers come, hoe the groves, and eat the olives. Is this proper or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story, connected only because אייבו is the same reporter. Here a man asks a question that sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation places the story in שביעית. In that year the land must rest, and the fruit must be ownerless. The villagers hoe his groves and in return eat his olives, so the שביעית fruit is acting like wages for their work instead of being truly ownerless. The fix in step 17 keeps hoeing but separates it from the fruit. This shows that the problem was this trade, not the hoeing itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They hoe (break up the soil around the trees)

phrases.english: Aivu said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק,
phrases.english: I was standing before Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ הָהוּא גַּבְרָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: a certain man came before him and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: קִרְיָיתָא אִית לִי, כַּרְמַיָּא אִית לִי, זֵיתַיָּא אִית לִי,
phrases.english: I have villages, I have groves, I have olives,
and the villagers come and hoe the groves
and eat from the olives —
is it appropriate or not appropriate?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַיְיבוּ: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק, אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ הָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected only by the same reporter, אייבו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it proper to let villagers hoe the groves and eat the olives during שביעית?

steps.title: It is not proper
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק answers that this situation is not proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not proper.
steps.whatsHappening: The sage gives a short answer to the man's question: what is happening on his land is not right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not yet say how to fix the problem. He only says the current situation is wrong. This leaves room for the follow-up question later in the story.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not appropriate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the man's question.

steps.title: The sage praises the man's honesty
steps.stepSummary: As the man walks away, רבי אלעזר בר צדוק says that in forty years in ארץ ישראל he has never seen anyone this careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the man was leaving, the sage said: I have lived in this land forty years, and I have never seen a person walk in such a straight path as this.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side comment in the story. The sage praises the man for being so careful about a problem other people would ignore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most owners would not worry about what villagers do on their land without permission. This man came to ask anyway. That is why the sage calls his path 'straight'. The praise also prepares for the man returning to ask what to do.

phrases.english: He was leaving him and going away.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כְּדוּ הֲוֵיתִי דָּיַיר בְּאַרְעָא הָדָא אַרְבְּעִין שְׁנִין,
phrases.english: He said: I have already lived in this land forty years,
and I have not seen a person
walking in paths as straight as this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A narrative comment after the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praise for the man's exceptional honesty.

steps.title: The man returns and asks what to do
steps.stepSummary: The man comes back and asks how he should fix the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came back and said to him: What should I do?
steps.whatsHappening: The man returns to ask for a practical solution. This sets up the sage's instructions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that something is wrong is not enough. He wants to know how to fix it. His question moves the story from 'is this proper?' to 'what is the remedy?'

phrases.aramaic: הָדַר וְאָתֵי וְאָמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי מֶיעְבַּד?
phrases.english: He came back and said to him: What should I do?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָדַר וְאָתֵי וְאָמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי מֶיעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question asking for a solution.

steps.title: Make the olives ownerless and pay workers to hoe
steps.stepSummary: The sage tells him to declare the olives הפקר for the poor and to pay workers to do the hoeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Make the olives ownerless for the poor, and give coins to workers to hoe the groves.
steps.whatsHappening: The sage gives a two-part fix. The fruit should be openly given up for the poor, and the hoeing should be done by paid workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית the fruit must be ownerless anyway, so he should openly declare it הפקר. The hoeing will be done properly by hired workers instead of by the villagers. This answer seems to allow hoeing in שביעית, and that triggers the next challenge.

phrases.english: He said to him: Declare the olives ownerless for the poor,
and give coins for hoeing the groves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what should I do' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Declare the olives הפקר for the poor and pay workers to hoe.

steps.title: But hoeing is forbidden in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the sage's advice. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that hoeing is forbidden in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is hoeing allowed? But a ברייתא teaches: 'The seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow.' 'Let it rest' means from hoeing, and 'lie fallow' means from clearing stones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the sage's instruction to pay workers to hoe. A ברייתא seems to say that hoeing is forbidden in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק's two words as two separate prohibitions. 'תשמטנה' forbids hoeing, and 'ונטשתה' forbids clearing stones. If hoeing is forbidden, how could רבי אלעזר בר צדוק tell the man to pay workers to hoe?

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא
To clear stones from a field

phrases.english: And is hoeing permitted?
But it was taught in a baraita:
"But the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow" (Exodus 23:11).
"You shall let it rest" — from hoeing,
"and lie fallow" — from clearing stones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the advice given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's instruction to pay workers to hoe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that hoeing is forbidden in שביעית.

steps.title: Two kinds of hoeing
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא answers that there are two kinds of hoeing. Hoeing to seal cracks is permitted, and hoeing to improve the trees is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא said: There are two kinds of hoeing. One seals cracks in the ground, and one strengthens the trees. Strengthening the trees is forbidden. Sealing cracks is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by dividing hoeing into two types. The ברייתא forbids one type, and the sage allowed the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sealing cracks only keeps the trees from being damaged or dying, so it is allowed. Hoeing to make the trees grow better is real farming work, so the ברייתא forbids it. The sage's advice referred to the permitted kind.
steps.whatToRemember: In שביעית, hoeing to protect trees (sealing cracks) is permitted. Hoeing to improve them is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said:
There are two kinds of hoeing.
One — to seal cracks,
and one — to strengthen the trees.
Strengthening the trees is forbidden;
sealing cracks is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: תְּרֵי קִשְׁקוּשֵׁי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא by distinguishing two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two types of the same activity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All hoeing is the same, so the advice contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids hoeing that improves the trees. The sage allowed hoeing that only seals cracks.

steps.title: Do not travel more than three פרסאות on Friday
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching from אייבו in the name of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק: a person should not walk more than three פרסאות on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אייבו said in the name of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק: A person should not walk on Fridays more than three פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching passed on by אייבו from the same sage, about travel on ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that you should arrive early enough for food to be ready for שבת. If you come home late without warning, your household has not prepared enough. The limit is three פרסאות.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַיְיבוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: Aivu said in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok:
A person should not walk on Shabbat eves
more than three parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַיְיבוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same reporter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not travel more than three פרסאות on ערב שבת.

steps.title: The limit applies only when going home
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא limits the rule. It applies only when going home. Someone going to an inn relies on the food he brought, so he may travel further.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: We only said this about someone going to his own house. But someone going to an inn relies on the food he took with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא narrows the previous rule. It covers only someone traveling home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At home, the family prepares only the usual amount, so a late arrival can leave everyone short of food. A traveler going to an inn knows he cannot count on the inn, so he carries his own food. The worry does not apply to him, and he may travel further.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only in the case of

steps.whatToRemember: The three-פרסאות limit on ערב שבת applies only when going home, not when going to an inn with your own food.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
We said this only regarding going to his house,
but going to his inn —
he relies on what he took with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְבֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the rule in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The travel limit applies only when going home. Someone going to an inn may travel further, because he relies on his own food.

steps.title: Second version: the rule applies even when going home
steps.stepSummary: In a second version (איכא דאמרי), רב כהנא says the three-פרסאות limit on ערב שבת applies even to someone traveling to his own house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב כהנא said: The rule was needed even for someone going to his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of what רב כהנא said. In this version he does not limit the rule. He extends it so that it also covers someone going home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 21), the rule applied only when going home, because at an inn the traveler relies on the food he brought. In this version the rule applies even going home. You cannot count on food being ready at home either. Going to an inn is surely included.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for: shows the new case the rule covers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In version one, רב כהנא says the rule applies ONLY when going home. In version two, he says it applies EVEN when going home. So in version two, going to an inn is certainly included.

phrases.english: And some say:
Rav Kahana said:
It was needed only to teach that it applies even to one going to his house.
phrases.notes: And all the more so to one going to an inn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב כהנא's statement that reverses the scope of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on traveling more than three פרסאות on ערב שבת applies even to one going home, and surely to one going to an inn.

steps.title: רב כהנא's own story: he found no food at home
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא tells of a time he traveled home on ערב שבת and found not even a small dish of fried fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It happened to me. I did not even find a dish of small fried fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא supports the second version with something that happened to him. Even at home, nothing was ready for him to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His story proves that a person cannot rely on his home having food when he arrives late on Friday. This supports applying the rule even to someone traveling home. The practical lesson is to arrive early enough to prepare for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish of small fish fried in oil, a cheap simple food

steps.whatToRemember: According to the second version, the three-פרסאות limit on ערב שבת applies to every traveler, even one going home. רב כהנא found nothing ready at home.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
There was an incident with me myself,
and even a dish of small fried fish
I did not find.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second version of רב כהנא's rule (step 22) with a personal story.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that even someone going home cannot count on food being ready on ערב שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's own experience of finding no food at home.

steps.title: New section: quoting the משנה on taking the לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the next part of the משנה: "How is the מצוה of לולב done?"
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the מצוה of לולב done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the travel topic. It returns to the משנה by quoting its words about how the לולב was handled in the בית המקדש when the first day of סוכות was on שבת. This line opens the new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the people's procedure. They brought their לולבים to the הר הבית on Friday. The attendants arranged them on a bench so each person could take his own on שבת. The גמרא quotes only the heading. It is about to discuss the exact wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of taking the לולב

phrases.english: How is the מצוה of lulav performed?
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the next topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא goes back to the משנה after finishing the side discussion on travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה describes how the לולב was taken in the מקדש when the first day of סוכות fell on שבת.

steps.title: A תנא's version: arranging them on the roof of the bench
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited the משנה before רב נחמן as "they arrange them on the roof of the bench". The גמרא then introduces רב נחמן's response.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: They arrange them on the roof of the bench. רב נחמן said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא, whose job was reciting משניות from memory, says the line with the words "on the roof of the bench". The last words, "he said to him", set up רב נחמן's reaction, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is the wording "גג האיצטבא", the roof (top) of the bench. רב נחמן is about to object to this wording and correct it. His response continues on the next amud. This step is the setup for his reaction.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter who memorized and recited משניות and ברייתות in the study hall

steps.confusionAlert: Here תנא does not mean a sage of the משנה. It means a professional reciter in the בית המדרש of the אמוראים.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Naḥman:
They arrange them on the roof of the bench.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: Sets up רב נחמן's response, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a recited version of the משנה just quoted, so that its wording can be examined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The recited text says the attendants arrange the לולבים on the "roof" of the bench, and this wording is about to be examined by רב נחמן.
